[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Desmond Ortiz, Senior Accountant, Tax (mid).
Senior tax accountant: complex S corps and the construction clients, first reviewer for staff work, unofficial mentor to every new hire including Maya.
Personality: Patient teacher, wry, never lets a diagnostic slide.
Email register: Friendly, concrete; signs 'Des'.
Chat register: Casual, helpful, links the exact workpaper.
Working hours: 08:30-17:30

[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Frank Osei
To: Desmond Ortiz
Subject: Job margin — need answers

Desmond,

This last job closed way under what we quoted. I need to know why. Get me the numbers — labor, materials, the whole breakdown. Don't sugarcoat it.

We can't keep bleeding like this. Let's figure it out and fix it.

Frank

---

From: Desmond Ortiz
To: Frank Osei
Subject: Re: Job margin — need answers

Frank,

Got it. I pulled the job file and ran the breakdown — no sugarcoating.

Labor came in about 12% over estimate, mostly overtime on the framing crew and a rework on the foundation pour. Materials were roughly 6% over — we paid a premium on lumber because of the late spec changes. Equipment rental ran about 3% over, and we had an unplanned dumpster haul-off fee that added another point.

Net: labor is the big leak. I've attached the detail by cost code if you want to dig in. I'd suggest we review the next two jobs' labor estimates against actuals weekly, and I can flag any variance over 5% before we get too deep.

Want me to set up a quick call to walk through the numbers?

Des

---

From: Frank Osei
To: Desmond Ortiz
Subject: Re: Job margin — need answers

Desmond,

Got your numbers. Labor is the leak. 12% over is not acceptable. The rework on the foundation pour is what worries me—that's a planning failure, not a cost of doing business.

Set up the call. We go through the breakdown line by line. Weekly variance checks starting now. Anything over 5%, I want to know before it bleeds.

Don't just flag it—tell me what we're doing to stop it.

Frank

[[ ## intent ## ]]
Answer Frank's follow-up on job margin breakdown with a concrete offer for a working session to walk through the numbers

[[ ## established_facts ## ]]
Requesting PBC workpapers from Cardinal Ridge Builders contact to begin 1120-S collection, listing specific documents and flagging major transactions.
Send formal PBC request to Cardinal Ridge Builders' contact, listing required workpapers (TB, GL, bank/credit statements, loans, fixed assets, payroll, K-1s, shareholder items) and flagging major transactions (asset sales, shareholder loans, large one-offs, accounting changes) to begin 1120-S collection.
Provides Frank with a breakdown of the job margin shortfall: labor 12% over, materials 6% over, equipment 3% over, plus an unplanned haul-off fee. Recommends weekly labor variance reviews and offers a call to walk through details.

[[ ## relevant_knowledge ## ]]
None.

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## draft ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python EmailDraft), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.
